content.thinking:
archiveMember already sets status to "suspended" and archives.

The "suspended" status is overloaded. Archived members currently receive it, but the task requires suspended members to keep their membership and seat while appearing in the member list. This creates a conflict with the existing archive logic.

I need to examine how activity listeners map member events, notification fan-out, digests, mentions, issue assignments, org lists, usage rollups, and seat counts.

findMemberById returns archived members, so suspend and reinstate must treat them as not found. removeMember should remain unchanged unless necessary. assertLastOwnerRetained needs to exclude suspended owners from the count. Suspending the only non-suspended owner must be refused.

Suspension and reinstatement require the actor's role to strictly outrank the member's. Equal roles are permitted except for self-suspension. Owners may suspend other owners. The member:remove permission is required.
The activity service does not subscribe to the member.

The task requires recording each item in the audit log as the actions member.

Suspended and reinstated member actions must be added to the ActivityAction type, schema, listeners, and labels. Suspended members will be excluded from all notifications and daily digests.
Seat counts are calculated by counting only members with an active status.
Reading the usage-repository seat query.

content.thinking:
archiveMember sets both the status to "suspended" and the archivedAt timestamp.

archiveMember must stay unchanged. Removed members are suspended but archived, so they should not count toward seat totals.

The seat count query should include suspended members while excluding archived ones. Existing tests for fresh tenants remain unaffected. The findMemberById function must check archivedAt to throw NotFoundError for removed members during suspend and reinstate operations.

Non-existent member IDs should throw NotFoundError. Self and outrank guards will use PermissionDeniedError, matching the existing member:remove permission check. These checks are new additions not present in removeMember.

Self and outrank guards will throw a generic Error, matching the pattern in updateMemberRole. The assertLastOwnerRetained helper must be updated to exclude suspended members when counting owners.

The last-owner guard now excludes suspended owners from the count. A suspended owner no longer protects the workspace, so demoting or removing an active member is refused when that owner is suspended. If the only remaining owner is suspended, demoting the last active owner is also refused.

The suspend operation will call assertLastOwnerRetained, which treats the next role as non-owner and checks remaining non-suspended owners. Idempotent calls return unchanged without publishing. The repository needs an updateMemberStatus method.

Session and resolveActor already exclude suspended members, so no changes are needed there. The listOrgsForUser query should filter for active member status to prevent suspended users from seeing workspaces. Currently invited members might appear if not archived, but the active status check will keep them out.

Invitations live in a separate table, so the active status filter correctly excludes suspended users from the workspace switcher.

The notify() function must skip suspended recipients. Digest generation should also exclude them in both listDigestRecipients and buildDigest, preventing old notifications from reaching suspended members.

Digests will skip suspended recipients without deleting their existing notifications. Reinstated members will then receive those old unread items in their next digest. The findMember lookup by userId already returns suspended members, so no extra filtering is needed there.

Issue assignment must verify the assignee is not suspended before writing. If the assignee is suspended, throw MemberSuspendedError. Do not add checks for unknown users. Check suspended status during createIssue and assignIssue, but only when an assignee is provided. Assigning an already-assigned suspended member should leave the existing assignment unchanged.

Re-assigning an issue to the same suspended member throws, even if the assignment already exists. Un-assigning and assigning to active members remain unchanged.

Mentions must filter suspended members from resolution lists and drop client-provided IDs whose member is suspended.

resolveMentionedUsers will filter suspended members from the mentionable set. Client-provided IDs are drawn only from that filtered list. Suspended members' handles will not resolve in issue bodies.

notify() must also suppress notifications for suspended authors, assignees, and comment watchers. No event fan-out or direct notify call should reach them.
